_note: Standard tank footprints (outer dimensions, inches). Notes are hand-written per size, not templated. Product picks are resolved in lib/tanks.ts from real catalogue fit ranges.

tanks.name: 5 gallon
tanks.summary: The classic desk nano. Small enough to light with one clip-on or a 40 cm bar, big enough for a shrimp colony and a carpet.
tanks.style: Nano shrimp tank or a single betta with a moss and crypt scape.
plants: Java moss and Christmas moss on wood
Cryptocoryne parva or wendtii in the foreground
Anubias nana petite tied to stone
Monte Carlo if you add DIY CO2
tanks.stocking: A colony of neocaridina shrimp, or one betta, or a small group of chili rasboras. Not all three: 19 litres crashes fast when you overstock it.
pitfalls: Heater too big. A 25 W unit is plenty; anything larger cooks a tank this small if the thermostat sticks.
Too much flow. Bettas and shrimp both hate a waterfall filter on full; a USB nano filter or sponge is the right size.
Dosing by the cap. Liquid fertilizer dose charts assume 40 L or more, so measure in drops, not caps.
faq: Is a 5 gallon tank big enough for live plants?
Yes. Low-light plants like moss, anubias and crypts grow well in 5 gallons with a small LED and no CO2. The limit is stability, not space: do 30% water changes weekly.

tanks.name: 10 gallon
tanks.summary: The most common first tank in North America, and a good one: a 50 cm footprint takes a single LED bar and a real hardscape.
tanks.style: Low-tech jungle or a small iwagumi with one main stone.
plants: Vallisneria or Sagittaria along the back glass
Java fern and Bucephalandra on driftwood
Dwarf sagittaria as an easy carpet
Rotala rotundifolia if you want red stems
tanks.stocking: A school of 8 to 10 small tetras or rasboras plus a few otocinclus or shrimp. Skip goldfish and anything that tops 2 inches.
pitfalls: Buying a hood light. Most kit lids hold a low-output bulb; plants need a full-spectrum bar of 15 W or more.
Soil too shallow. Aim for about 2 inches at the front and 3 at the back so roots have somewhere to go.
Skipping the photoperiod. Six to seven hours on a timer stops most algae before it starts.
faq: Do I need CO2 for a 10 gallon planted tank?
No. A 10 gallon grows moss, ferns, crypts and easy stems without CO2. Add it only if you want a dense carpet or fast red stems.

tanks.name: 20 gallon long
tanks.summary: Shallow and wide, which is exactly what plants want: light reaches the substrate easily and the 30 inch length gives you room for a real layout.
tanks.style: Nature aquarium with a sloped hardscape, or a shallow riverbank scape.
plants: Monte Carlo or dwarf hairgrass carpet (CO2 helps)
Staurogyne repens in the midground
Ludwigia and Rotala stems at the back
Floating red root floaters to shade shy fish
tanks.stocking: A school of 12 ember tetras or harlequin rasboras, a group of pygmy corydoras on sand, and shrimp for clean-up.
pitfalls: Choosing a 60 cm light. The tank is 76 cm long, so a short bar leaves dark ends; use a bar that fits 70 to 95 cm.
Under-sloping. A shallow tank looks flat unless the substrate rises 2 inches from front to back.
Heater placement. Put it near the filter outflow so warm water reaches both ends of a long tank.
faq: Is a 20 long better than a 20 high for plants?
Usually yes. The 20 long is 12 inches tall, so light reaches the bottom at full strength and carpet plants grow without high-output lighting.

tanks.name: 20 gallon high
tanks.summary: A taller column of water on a smaller footprint. Great for stem plants and vertical wood, harder for carpets.
tanks.style: Vertical driftwood scape with tall stems and epiphytes.
plants: Tall stems: Limnophila, Hygrophila, Rotala
Spider wood with java fern and moss climbing it
Cryptocoryne wendtii in the shade under wood
Amazon frogbit to soften the light
tanks.stocking: Mid-water swimmers suit the height: a pair of honey gouramis with a school of 10 lemon tetras.
pitfalls: Expecting a carpet. At 16 inches tall, light at the substrate drops off; pick plants that tolerate shade at the bottom.
Weak circulation. Tall tanks stratify; point the filter return along the surface so water rolls top to bottom.
Short light. The tank is 61 cm long; a 48 to 61 cm bar is the right fit.
faq: Can you carpet a 20 gallon high?
It is harder than a 20 long because the substrate sits 16 inches from the light. Use a stronger light and CO2, or choose shade-tolerant ground cover like crypts.

tanks.name: 29 gallon
tanks.summary: A 20 long footprint with 6 extra inches of height. More water stability and fish options, but the light has further to travel.
tanks.style: Community planted tank with background stems and an open swimming area.
plants: Amazon sword as a centrepiece (feed it root tabs)
Cryptocoryne and Anubias in the lower third
Hygrophila polysperma and Bacopa along the back
Java moss on a log for fry cover
tanks.stocking: A school of 12 to 15 rummy-nose or cardinal tetras, a group of 6 corydoras, and a pair of dwarf cichlids or a centrepiece gourami.
pitfalls: One weak light. 18 inches of water dims a small bar; use a bar rated for a 76 cm tank at full power or run two.
Overfeeding a big school. Uneaten food is the fastest route to an algae outbreak in a newly planted 29.
Undersized filter. Aim for about 4 to 6 times the tank volume per hour, which is more than most 20 gallon filters move.
faq: What light do I need for a 29 gallon planted tank?
A full-spectrum bar that covers the 30 inch (76 cm) length. Because the tank is 18 inches tall, run it at full output or add a second bar if you want carpet plants.

tanks.name: 40 gallon breeder
tanks.summary: The aquascaper favourite: 18 inches front to back gives real depth to a layout, and 16 inches of height keeps light at the substrate.
tanks.style: Full nature aquarium or iwagumi with a deep foreground and layered hardscape.
plants: Dwarf hairgrass or Eleocharis carpet
Bucephalandra and Anubias on rockwork
Rotala and Ludwigia groups for colour at the back
Cryptocoryne along the hardscape edges
tanks.stocking: A large school (20 or more) of one small species reads best in an aquascape, plus otocinclus and amano shrimp for algae.
pitfalls: Single light on a deep tank. 18 inches front to back leaves the back row dim with one bar; run two or mount one at the centre line.
Not enough rock. A convincing layout in 40 gallons needs more hardscape than people expect; buy for the layout, then remove.
CO2 under-dosed. At 150 litres, a small DIY bottle runs out quickly; a pressurised regulator is easier to keep stable.
faq: How much substrate do I need for a 40 breeder?
About 3 inches on average (2 at the front, 4 at the back) is roughly 30 litres of aqua soil. See the substrate figures on this page for the exact number at other depths.

tanks.name: 55 gallon
tanks.summary: Long, narrow and tall. A forgiving volume for fish, but the 21 inch height and 48 inch length make lighting the main decision.
tanks.style: Large community planted tank with background jungle and open midwater.
plants: Vallisneria and Amazon swords at the back
Java fern, Anubias and Bucephalandra on wood
Cryptocoryne and Marsilea in the foreground
Floating plants to tame the light on a tall tank
tanks.stocking: Room for a school of 20 tetras, a group of 8 corydoras or a bristlenose pleco, and a centrepiece such as a pair of angelfish.
pitfalls: Light that does not span the tank. You need about 120 cm of coverage; a short bar leaves both ends dark.
Thin substrate. 48 inches of footprint takes a lot of soil; budget for it before you buy plants.
Single small heater. Two smaller heaters at each end hold temperature better than one large unit.
faq: Can a 55 gallon planted tank work without CO2?
Yes, with low-light plants: ferns, anubias, crypts, swords and vallisneria. The height means fast stems and carpets will struggle without CO2 and strong light.

tanks.name: 60P (60 x 30 x 36 cm)
tanks.summary: The rimless 60 cm standard most aquascape contests and tutorials use. 64 litres, ultra-clear glass, nothing to hide behind.
tanks.style: Iwagumi or nature aquarium built for a rimless, open-top display.
plants: Monte Carlo or Glossostigma carpet with CO2
Hemianthus callitrichoides for advanced carpets
Rotala wallichii and Ludwigia for a red accent
Mini Bucephalandra on the main stones
tanks.stocking: A single school of 15 small fish such as ember tetras or green neons, plus amano shrimp. Keep it to one species for a clean look.
pitfalls: Visible equipment. On a rimless tank every pipe shows; glass lily pipes and a clear drop checker keep it clean.
Skipping the dry start or the high-CO2 start. Carpets in a 60P fill in weeks with CO2 from day one, months without.
Light overhang. A 60 cm tank needs a bar that fits 48 to 61 cm, mounted with legs, not a clip.
faq: 60 x 30 x 36 cm, or about 23.6 x 11.8 x 14.2 inches. That is 64 litres (17 US gallons) gross, around 55 litres of water once substrate and rock go in.
